jobs.description: The German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke (DIfE) (https://www.dife.de/en/) is a member of the Leibniz Association. The institute’s mission is to conduct experimental and clinical research in the field of nutrition and health, with the aim of understanding the molecular basis of nutrition-dependent diseases, and of developing new strategies for treatment and prevention.The Junior Research Group of Gut-Brain Interactions (GBI) (https://www.dife.de/en/research/departments-and-labs/gut-brain-interactions/)  invites applications for1 Postdoc (m/f/d)starting May 1, 2027.Project descriptionThe project investigates how signals from the stomach interact with brain systems supporting arousal, attention and cognition. Combining electrogastrography (EGG) with EEG, fMRI and peripheral physiology, we study the neural dynamics of stomach–brain coupling in healthy individuals. A central aim is to determine whether experimentally induced changes in arousal influence gastric–brain coupling independently of changes in gastric activity, and how these dynamics relate to vigilance and behaviour. The postdoc will lead electrophysiological and multimodal analyses, contribute to experiments involving pharmacological and physiological manipulations, and have scope to develop an independent research line within the programme.Skills and Requirements- Excellent Master degree and doctoral degree in the areas of Psychology, Cognitive Neuroscience or Biology- Strong background in electrophysiology (EEG, MEG, Intracranial EEG) and/or strong background in neuroimaging (fMRI data analysis, SPM, FSL)- Solid understanding of statistics and signal processing and Python/Matlab- High motivation for interdisciplinary research on brain–body interactions- Experience with physiological data (EGG, ECG, Respiration, Pupil) or Psychophysics is an asset- Proficiency in English (spoken and written)- Very high motivation and willingness for interdisciplinary collaboration in a diverse research environmentWe offer:- Excellent technical equipment, a wide range of experimental methods and a dynamic and interactive research environment- Remuneration according to TV-L, level 13, plus annual special payment and company pension scheme- Family-friendly working conditions (certificate “audit berufundfamilie”)- Supporting of mobility with a jobticket for using the public transport- Easy accessibility by public transport or car (including free parking)- 30 days of vacation- Participation in the benefits program for employees („Corporate Benefits“)The advertised position is available for 1 year with the option of extension.We promote the employment of people with severe disabilities and are committed to equal opportunities for them. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications.Please send your documents (cover letter explaining your motivation, CV, copies of degrees/certificates and references) with reference number 2026_W11_BA as a single pdf-file before November 30, 2026 via e-mail to jobs@dife.de (https://mailto:jobs@dife.de) . For further information please do not hesitate to contact: Dr. Ignacio RebolloHead of Junior Research Group Gut Brain Interactions (GBI)E-Mail: Ignacio.Rebollo@dife.de (https://mailto:Ignacio.Rebollo@dife.de)  We process your application documents for the purpose of carrying out the application procedure in accordance with Art. 6 para. 1 lit. b) GDPR, Art. 88 GDPR. For more information on the collection, processing and use of personal data by the German Institute of Human Nutrition as part of the application process and your rights under data protection law, please contact the Department of Human Resources and Social Services (jobs@dife.de (https://mailto:jobs@dife.de) ).Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: StatistikErweiterte Kenntnisse: Psychologie, Neurobiologie, Neurowissenschaften (Neuroscience), Neurophysiologie

PhD Position (E13, 65%) in Tumor ImmunologyThe Chair for Infection Pathogenesis is looking for academic staff, starting as soon as possible.BackgroundWe are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate (E13, 65%) to join a DFG-funded research project investigating the role of tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) in intestinal polyp dynamics in a pig model. The pig model provides an excellent opportunity to explore the diverse facets of comparative immunology and to bridge fundamental immunological mechanisms with translational research.This project aims to elucidate the function of TANs on polyp growth and regression with a particular focus on their interaction with the local tissue microenvironment and immune response. A key component of the project will be the establishment and use of intestinal organoid–neutrophil co-culture models to study TAN-mediated effects on epithelial and polyp cells. The successful candidate will work in an interdisciplinary research environment using state-of-the-art molecular, cellular, immunological, and organoid-based approaches.Your responsibilitiesThe successful candidate will plan and conduct experimental studies investigating TAN phenotypes and functions during intestinal polyp development. The work combines in vivo studies using transgenic animal models, including animal breeding, sample collection, and histopathological analyses, with in vitro organoid–immune cell co-culture systems and molecular, cellular and immunological assays. The candidate will analyse and interpret the resulting data, present findings at scientific meetings, and contribute to manuscripts and reports. Independent experimental work, careful sample handling, and a high level of scientific responsibility are expected.Your qualifications, key skills and experience- Master’s degree or Staatsexamen or equivalent in Veterinary Medicine, Animal sciences, Medicine, Biology, Biotechnology or related fields- Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international team- Strong interest in tumour immunology, inflammation, and gastrointestinal disease- Experience with molecular biology, flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, cell culture, or animal models is advantageous- Very good written and spoken English, Strong analysis and problem-solving capacitiesWhat we offerThe candidate will have the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary and international scientific environment. Research staff is supported by easy access to scientific expertise, well-equipped lab and core facilities and an active science community @Weihenstephan Campus. We offer a three-year PhD position funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and an employment according to TV-L E13 (65%).Your applicationIf you are interested in working in our team, please send your application by mail together with a strong CV and supporting documentation to the Chair of Infection Pathogenesis* (friederike.ebner@tum.de)*.Technische Universität MünchenSchool of Life Sciences – Infection PathogenesisProf. Dr. rer. nat.
